about: FIXTURE copy of SPEC.json for tool tests. Same keys as aws-saa-book/_build/style/SPEC.json, with tiny limits and counts so that the miniature chapter 99-sample passes. Only the deep template is present; chapter_overrides is empty.

resolution.template: template key = chapter.kind when the registry entry has one (pattern), else chapter.tier (deep, medium, light, front, synthesis, mock). If chapter_overrides[<chapter id>] has `template`, that template replaces the tier template. Then the override is merged on top: objects merge key by key, recursively; arrays (for example `files`) and scalars are replaced as a whole. One function resolves it for every module: lint.template(ch)
resolution.section_key: `key` names a template section inside SPEC.json only (headings.fixed_h3 and bold_fields refer to it). The section id used everywhere else (JSON items, brief.json, fact requests, lint.sections, web routes, progress keys) is headings.section_id: the heading anchor without the time box
resolution.section_requires: a section must hold only what its `counts`, `fields` and `subsection_fields` name; a role adds grounding rules, never devices
resolution.words: a words object is {min, max}; xl_max replaces max when chapter.xl is true; by_tier.<tier> replaces the whole object for that tier; min 0 means no minimum
resolution.counts: a count is either a number (exact) or {min, max}; an empty object counts nothing; a row count is the sum over all tables of that kind in the section
resolution.word_count: count whitespace-separated tokens that contain a letter or digit, after removing front matter, HTML comments, fenced code, generated regions and link targets; link text, table cells, callouts, AWS quote blocks and text inside details blocks (reveals and Go deeper) count toward file and section limits
resolution.minutes: templates.<template>.minutes are planning targets, not rules; lint checks the front matter minutes against lint.minutes_formula

startup.name: Callvale
startup.story_counts: the words of the Startup example callouts of the chapter's hand files; the Decision record has its own section limit

front_matter.syntax: between two lines of ---; one key per line; value is a scalar, a flow list [a, b] or a flow map {k: v}; no multi-line values; quote strings that are digits or contain a colon
front_matter.status_written_by: `stage end`: draft when prose passes, reviewed when fix passes, ready when finalize passes; a writer never changes status

section_flag.service_key: required on service cards in 2-services.md; the value is a service key of the chapter's registry entry
section_flag.position: the line directly after the H2, followed by a blank line

grounding.strict: a sentence or table cell with a number-with-unit or an absolute word needs a fact link in the same sentence or cell; each hard fact is its own link
grounding.example: story and example values are allowed without fact links (RULINGS: roles example, task, worked; prompts are example blocks); link AWS facts here too when the text states one, although the lint does not require it
grounding.heuristic: advice about the exam or about study method: absolute words are allowed; a number-with-unit needs a fact link, except a time unit of heuristic_exempt_units in a sentence that holds no word of exam_fact_words (the book's own study times)
example_blocks: prompt paragraph (its bold label is a key of prompts.labels)
text between **Wrong belief:** and **Truth:** in a traps item
cells of a plan or log table
bold field:Problem. of a pattern card
bold field:Requirement. of an architecture page
text in straight double quotes at the start of an Exam signal callout
text in straight double quotes directly after questions.twin_prefix
heuristic_blocks: the line that starts **The exam probably expects:** in a Changed recently entry
columns 1 and 3 of a signals table (Think, But not if)
skips: H2 and H3 heading lines (see headings.grounding)
bold labels of prompts, bold fields and callouts
grounding.no_fact_rule: at the end of a sentence or cell: the lint accepts the sentence without a fact link, reports the marker as W308, and the claims reviewer checks every use; requirement = the sentence states what a workload or customer needs, stem = it restates a stem condition, plan = a number of her own study plan
exempt_sentences: No change since July 2022 affects an answer in this chapter.

files.name: 2-services.md
files.present_when: the registry entry has a non-empty `cards` list
files.sections_ref: templates.light.files[1].sections: one card per service key in the registry entry's `cards` list

headings.h1: exactly one, equal to the front matter title; any characters
time_box_required_on: every H3 inside a section with role how
every H3 of a section whose counts name `subsections`
headings.assertion_headings_apply_to: H3 subsections of a section with role how, unless the section has assertion_headings false
headings.fixed_h3_keyed_by: template section key (not role): only sections whose key is signals or numbers carry these H3; a section with another key (46 top-traps, 47 a-list) has no H3
headings.fixed_h3_optional_rule: leave the B-list H3 out when it has no row
headings.grounding: body-link: a heading line is never checked by L304 (a heading cannot hold a link). An H2 or H3 heading that has a number with a unit or an absolute word needs at least one fact link in the body of its own section or subsection (L308); the claims reviewer checks that the link grounds the heading
headings.unique_section_ids: a section id is unique in the chapter folder, over all hand files (L108)
headings.section_id: GitHub anchor of the heading text without the time box: lowercase, drop every character that is not a letter, digit, space or hyphen, then spaces become hyphens
headings.markdown_anchor: GitHub anchor of the full heading text including the time box, for links inside Markdown

callouts.not_counted_reason: one Say it and one Exam signal (or the Exam heuristic that replaces it) per How-it-works subsection
callouts.label_rule: the label of a callout is the bold text at the start of the first line of the blockquote; later lines of the same blockquote are not labels
callouts.exam_trap_id: an Exam trap callout in 2-deep.md can end with <!-- trap: <trap id> -->; lint.traps() collects trap ids from the traps lists and from these callouts

labels.label: Key fact
labels.use: the one fact of a subsection that decides answers; optional

labels.label: Exam signal
labels.use: a stem phrase in straight double quotes (an example block), then what it points to and why (strict text)

labels.label: Exam trap
labels.use: a wrong belief and the truth

labels.label: Exam heuristic
labels.use: advice about the exam that AWS does not publish

labels.label: Changed recently
labels.use: a Changed recently entry; the text starts with a date in parentheses

labels.label: Say it
labels.use: a sentence to say aloud; the first one in In one breath is the one-breath definition; in How it works, one per subsection, directly before the Stop and answer, with the starters The short answer is and The thing to watch is

labels.label: Try it
labels.use: pointer to a task in 3-do.md; ends with a task comment

labels.label: Startup example
labels.use: the running startup; story values are allowed

changed_recently.cutoff_source: book.exam_eligibility_cutoff in data/book.json (the one source): an entry whose date is after the cut-off has Status `not examinable yet`
changed_recently.line_break_rule:
each of the first four lines of the blockquote ends with
, so that the five lines render as five lines
changed_recently.date_rule: the entry date equals changed.date of the fact that is linked in the Now: line
changed_recently.placement: an examinable entry stands in the Changed recently section of 1-fast.md; an entry with Status `not examinable yet` stands in 2-deep.md, directly under the B-list of Numbers that decide answers, next to the row of its number

prompts.syntax: a prompt is a paragraph whose bold label matches a key of `labels` (<n> = digits). Only prompts are example blocks. A bold field is a paragraph whose label is in bold_fields or in a template `fields` or `subsection_fields` list; a bold field is strict text in a strict role unless grounding.example_blocks names it. Any other paragraph that starts with bold text is plain text
prompts.intro_line: a Predict section can start with one plain line (at most 15 words) that says where the answers are
prompts.check_answers_predict: the reveal of Check <n> also answers Predict <n>, in one sentence
prompts.recap_rule: each Recap prompt asks for a sentence, row or cell that 1-fast.md states above it

FAQ <n>..answer: details:Answer with one AWS quote block

bold_fields.keyed_by: template section key, except traps (the traps list), figure (every diagram embed), card, pattern, page and atlas (the repeated sections of those roles)
question: The problem it solves.

devices.subsection_words_count: paragraphs, lists, tables and callouts of the subsection; not Go deeper blocks, prompts, reveals or code
devices.words_table: cell 1 is `<term>` or `<term> (<respelling>)`: the lint removes each part in parentheses, collapses spaces and compares with `term` of data/terms.json without regard to case. Cell 2 is one of the term's `collocations` with exactly one bold span, the partner word. Cells 3 and 4 are free text that must not contradict the bank
devices.term_definition: in 1-fast.md the words table is the definition; the five steps of STYLE section 2 apply at the first use of a term in 2-deep.md
devices.pass_route_criterion: mark the How it works subsections that the core questions review
devices.try_it: every Try and Lab has exactly one Try it callout, in the section that its `section` names

tables.kind_comment_position: the line directly before the header row
tables.rows_max_rule: the default for one table; a kind with its own rows_max replaces it. A section whose row count is above the limit splits the rows over several tables of the same kind, each under its own H3

fact_links.service_must_equal_file_stem: the `service` field of the linked fact equals the file stem; a fact id of service X never starts with `<Y>-` for another service key Y that is longer than X (so iam-identity-center-... is not a fact of service iam)
fact_links.number_free_display_rule: a display without a digit is a verbatim phrase of at most 8 words
fact_links.comparison: normalize_text on both sides (case-insensitive; punctuation is kept), then substring; a display that starts or ends with a digit must not touch another digit of a longer number (`45 Gbps` does not hold `5 Gbps`; lint.holds_display)
fact_links.marker_severity: needs-display and needs-term follow needs_fact_severity (W307 in draft, L307 from reviewed)

aws_quote.match: strip the leading `> ` and the first and the last straight double quote of the quote line, then common.find_quote inside the evidence quote; copy the span exactly, punctuation included; the span can be a part of the evidence quote
aws_quote.case_study_quote_is: a quote whose matching fact has kind case-study
aws_quote.page: any saved AWS page; prefer the service FAQ for FAQ quick-fire items

external_allowed_in: Source. field of a service card
links.xref_rule: never link to a chapter that is not written yet; put the marker after the sentence. The lint reports each marker as W601; `lint --all --strict` (the whole-book pass, W14) makes it an error, and by then every marker is replaced by a real link
links.anchors_after_a_retimed_section: a changed time box changes the Markdown anchor; `lint --all` reports the broken links of other chapters as L601

diagram_embed.step_list: ordered list directly after the caption; one item per numbered step of the spec
diagram_embed.hero_inside: details:Show the picture after a Predict the picture. prompt
diagram_embed.equals_spec: when diagrams/src/<id>.json exists: the alt text equals the spec `alt`, the caption equals the spec `claim` and each step sentence equals the spec `say` of that step, compared after replacing links by their text and after normalize_text
diagram_embed.source_of_text: brief.json `diagrams` holds id, kind, claim, alt and say for each diagram; the prose writer and the diagram agent both copy from it
diagram_embed.grounding: the caption and the step sentences are strict text and can hold fact links; a spec `claim` or `say` with a number with a unit or an absolute word is grounded by the fact link of the equal Markdown sentence (L705 when that sentence has none)

region_keys.task: id=<task id> (in 1-fast.md: a look task; in 3-do.md: every task)

generated_regions.generated_file_first_line: <!-- generated by saa.py; do not edit -->

code.allowed_account_ids_rule: the 12-digit ban does not fire on these documentation account ids inside a fenced json block
code.placeholder_rule: a value that she must fill in is an uppercase placeholder in angle brackets, for example <ACCOUNT_ID> or <ROLE_ARN>, explained in the text next to the block

sentence.split: end a sentence at . ? ! or : followed by whitespace and an uppercase letter, digit, quote or end of block; a table cell and a list item are each at least one sentence

lint.absolute_word_match: case-insensitive; the word or phrase is not preceded and not followed by a letter, a digit or a hyphen (so read-only, append-only and must-have do not match)

number_with_unit.match: the number regex, then an optional space or hyphen, then a unit (case-sensitive) or a count noun (case-insensitive), then no further letter: `5 GB`, `5GB` and `10-second` all match; a currency amount always matches
number_with_unit.number_words: facts are written with digits; a small story count can be a word (`three laptops`); a number word is not matched by L304
exempt: Predict, Check, Recap and FAQ prompt numbers

lint.banned_words_scope: prose of hand-written files and every text field of JSON items except question stem and option text (exam register) and AWS quotes
lint.word_match: a banned word, a warn word, a customer word and a banned term variant match as (?<![A-Za-z0-9-])<phrase>(?![A-Za-z0-9-]), case-insensitive; `may` matches in lowercase only (the month May is not a match)

warn_words.over: use more than before a number

warn_word_rules.as: not checked (too frequent in `such as` and `the same as`); the reader lens reviews `as` for cause

customer_words_allowed_in: where the word is a `term` of data/terms.json with kind aws-name or concept
the prompt of a speak item
lint.customer_words_rule: L801 does not fire on a customer word inside one of its allowed places
lint.banned_term_match: L901: `banned` entries match with word_match; `banned_case` entries match case-sensitively; `avoid` entries are not matched. A variant does not match where it is part of a longer `term`, `short` or official service name at that place (`balancer` inside `load balancer`)
lint.abbreviation_rule: the short forms are the `short` values of data/terms.json; an official service name (kind aws-name) and the H1 are exempt
lint.term_rules: W901: the first occurrence of a term of data/terms.json in the chapter's hand files, in file order, is bold (or is cell 1 of a words table) and is followed by `(respelling)` when the term has one. W202 counts as new bold terms the bold spans that equal a term of the bank. Every word in bold as a definition and every row of a words table is a term of the bank; other AWS nouns are free
lint.orphan_rule: every How it works subsection is the section of at least one question, card, speak item or task

cause_codes.W: missed a word in the stem
cause_codes.D: dated question that assumes an old limit

minutes_formula.fast: the sum of the H2 time boxes of 1-fast.md (blocking, L105)
minutes_formula.pass: fast + the time boxes of the H3 subsections marked route=pass + the minutes of the Try with pass_route true + minutes_per_question x the core questions shipped + minutes_per_spoken_answer x the speak items with pass_route true
minutes_formula.full: fast + the H2 time boxes of 2-deep.md + the minutes of every Try and Lab + minutes_per_question x the questions shipped + minutes_per_spoken_answer x the speak items
minutes_formula.time_box: guidance for the writer, not checked: a time box is the words of the section divided by reading_words_per_minute, plus 1 minute for each prompt, rounded up to a whole minute; at least 1
minutes_formula.rounding: round half up to a whole minute
minutes_formula.severity: W105 when front matter pass or full differs from the formula by more than the tolerance; the lint report prints the computed values
minutes_formula.fast_check: W105 when the time_box guidance over 1-fast.md exceeds minutes.fast by more than tolerance_minutes (not implemented)

questions.twin_rules: the later question of a twin pair carries twin_of and the earlier has null; both have the same layer; the `twin` line of a question that has a real twin quotes the changed phrase of that twin
worked_step_starters: I read the last sentence first: it asks for
Before I look at the options, I predict
questions.worked_wrong_path_rule: with wrong_path true, step 3 states the plausible wrong prediction and step 5 holds one sentence that starts with the marker; with wrong_path false the marker is absent
questions.violates_qualifier_rule: a question of difficulty 2 or 3 has a qualifier and at least one violates-qualifier option; a question with qualifier none has no violates-qualifier option
questions.options_rule: four options for a single answer, five for (Select TWO.), six for (Select THREE.); `keywords` can include the qualifier phrase; the `why` of a correct option says why it is right (the app shows it after the answer, and it prints per option for a multiple-response question)
questions.layers: core = the questions of the brief slots with layer core (difficulty 1 or 2, one per bullet that the brief marks as must-know); extended = the others
questions.bullets_rule: a question of pool chapter or drill lists at least one bullet of its task (Q116)
questions.drill_pool: a drill question lives in the questions.json of its topic chapter, needs the same verification, is not counted by Q201 and is not printed in 5-quiz.md
questions.sources_rule: `sources` is for extra pages and is usually empty (sources.md is derived from the facts); each URL is in the corpus or is an evidence URL of a fact in `facts`
questions.volatile_rule: `q add` sets `volatile` to true when a fact that is linked in `explanation` or in the `why` of a correct option is volatile (facts.is_volatile); `facts amend` and `freshen` set it again on dependents. A question with `volatile` true is a Q112 error in every pool: rewrite it so that the changed value does not decide the key
questions.exam_english_match: an id in `exam_english` counts when its `word` or one of its `also` forms stands in the stem, without regard to case; `q words --need` lists the words below the minimum
questions.example_text_rule: a think-aloud is example text (RULINGS: role worked): no fact link is required, links are allowed, and every AWS fact that a step states is a fact of the question's `facts`
questions.strict_field_content: strict fields hold plain text and fact links only: no other Markdown, no other link

speak.digits_allowed_rule: a digit is also allowed when it is part of, or directly follows, a `term` or `short` of data/terms.json or an official service name (Route 53, gp3)
speak.compare_rule: in a compare prompt a first sentence that starts with `Both ` replaces the first starter; the other three starters keep their order
speak.spoken_number_rule: P109: in a script, a number word that is followed in the same sentence by a unit or a count noun (lint.number_with_unit, also in the singular) stands inside a `spoken` string of a fact in `facts`; copy the spoken form from the fact card. A number with a unit in key_points[].point, must_not_say[].correct or follow_ups[].answer stands inside a `display` of a fact of the item (for a follow-up: of its own `facts`)
speak.pack_set_by: the orchestrator (`speak set-pack`); writers set pack false
speak.recover_pattern: What I know is... What I would confirm is... I will check and come back to you today.

cards.generated_rule: `cards build` writes the generated cards with generated true and status ready; a writer never writes a generated type, and `cards add` refuses one. templates.<template>.counts.cards counts hand types only. A say card has back = ten_second and extra = the skeleton cues joined with ` / `. data/cards-terms.json uses the wrapper with chapter `glossary` and ids glossary-c<3 digits>
cards.a_list_rule: every A-list row of a chapter has one number card (C204)
cards.number_in_text_rule: C109: a number with a unit in `front` or `back` stands inside a `display` of a fact in `facts`

tasks.label: checked against docs, not run in a real account
tasks.tag_meaning: `tag` and `tag_task` name the tag key and value; a command writes them in the tag syntax of its service. T106 and T108 pass when one pattern of the lists below matches (regular expressions; <task id> is replaced by the id)
tasks.verify_rule: the verify command filters by the task tag; T108 replaces <task id> as T106 does
tasks.tag_patterns_status: the service tag syntaxes behind these patterns come from memory; `tasks check-cli --reference` confirms each command against the CLI reference in the corpus before a task ships
tasks.untaggable_rule: T106 skips an operation of this list; the step, or the next step, then tags the resource with its own tagging operation, or the resource name starts with name_prefix. The list is a seed: `tasks check-cli` warns (T118) when the CLI model shows a tag option for a listed operation, or none for an unlisted create operation
tasks.stop_rule: At twice the stated time, run the cleanup and move on.
tasks.break_it_order: predict, break, observe (expect), explain; the fix is the next step
tasks.read_only_tools_rule: `curl` and `dig` are read-only checks: a curl command has none of -X, -d, --data, -T, -o, -O and uses https:// (or the instance metadata address)
tasks.banned_command_note: create-user is banned because STYLE section 8 rule 1 allows no IAM users in tasks; an IAM user is shown read-only (list-users, get-user)
tasks.create_command_applies_to: the operation only: the third word of an `aws <service> <operation>` command, never an option such as --launch-template or --copy-source

data_files.not_used: data/glossary.json (named in RULINGS) is not used: glossary.md is generated from data/terms.json
